student_group: Black, Asian, mixed and other heritage students
intervention: Provide bespoke support workshops and online training packages from level 3 in academic skills, English for Academic Purposes (EAP) for students where English is a second or other language, and digital literacy skills; inclusive assessment strategy allowing assessment choice; culturally diverse business and community leaders guest seminars and lectures; student mentorship schemes; parent and carer support.
intended_outcome: Eliminate gaps in attainment and ethnicity degree awarding gap between black and white students; improve cognitive and metacognitive outcomes, motivation, engagement, self-perceptions about belonging, academic abilities and confidence in academic practice, digital literacy and English proficiency; improve module/assessment grades, continuation, completion and progression rates; increase professional networks and career readiness; improve student emotional and mental wellbeing.
evaluation_approach: Process evaluation with Theory of Change models, data analysis of engagement and outcomes, output analysis of sessions run, post-activity polls, annual staff surveys, baseline and annual student surveys on academic skills and wellbeing, impact evaluation of continuation, completion, attainment rates and progression into employment or postgraduate study; comparative analysis between students who engaged and those who have not; involvement of student representatives in design and evaluation; membership in SEER network for research and evaluation expertise; ongoing monitoring and reflection for improvement.
supporting_quote:
Intervention strategy 1 – Enhanced Support and Access Pathways: Provide bespoke support workshops and online training packages... inclusive assessment strategy... culturally diverse business and community leaders guest seminars and lectures... student mentorship scheme... parent and carer support... Intermediate outcomes: Improved cognitive and metacognitive outcomes; Improved motivation and engagement in learning; Improved self-perceptions about belonging, academic abilities and confidence; Improved module / assessment grades; Increased knowledge and capacity relating to career and employability skills; Improved continuation, completion and progression rates.
Evaluation includes theory of change, data analysis, surveys, polls and comparative analyses with student involvement and external evaluation support from SEER.

student_group: Students from the most deprived areas (IMD quintiles 1 and 2), including males from these areas
intervention: Targeted academic and personal support workshops focusing on academic skills, emotional wellbeing and development (e.g. resilience, mindfulness, mental health awareness), mentor schemes pairing level 6 students from deprived areas with level 4 students, subsidised affordable food, travel support, late opening warm study spaces, and support for parents/carers.
intended_outcome: Eliminate attainment gaps between students from most deprived areas and those from least deprived; improve motivation, engagement, self-perceptions of academic abilities and confidence; improve emotional and mental wellbeing; improve module and assessment grades; improve continuation, completion and progression rates; reduce financial pressures and associated anxieties.
evaluation_approach: Theory of Change models, data analysis of student engagement and outcomes, output analysis of sessions run, post-activity student experience polls, annual staff surveys, baseline and annual student surveys for perceptions and confidence, and comparative analysis between those engaged and not; student involvement in evaluation and feedback loops facilitated through committees and feedback mechanisms; ongoing monitoring and continuous improvement with support from SEER.
supporting_quote: Intervention strategy 2 – Enhanced Support to Address Disadvantage: Delivery of workshops focusing on academic skills, mindset, and emotional wellbeing; student mentorship scheme; subsidised affordable food, travel support, and study spaces; parent and carer support... Outcomes include improved continuation rates, completion and attainment rates, improved motivation and engagement, improved student emotional and mental wellbeing, and reduced financial pressure/anxiety. Evaluation based on process and impact measures, student feedback, and Theory of Change.

student_group: All HE students
intervention: Full lifecycle approach including summer schools, academic writing workshops pre-entry; inclusive assessment strategies on programme; employability team access up to 3 years post-graduation; student consultation via surveys and focus groups; recruitment of ‘Widening Participation Fellows’ from intervention groups for design, monitoring and feedback; student partnership and engagement committees; promotional campaigns and student voice mechanisms; inclusion initiatives such as Project360 to enhance continuation, completion and progression.
intended_outcome: Reduce barriers to access and participation; improve student engagement, continuation, completion, progression; enhance student voice influence on provision; promote inclusion and psychological safety.
evaluation_approach: Ongoing monitoring and evaluation of intervention strategies; collaboration between academic teams, data teams and student representatives; use of student feedback and surveys; involvement in research and evaluation networks such as SEER; embedding evaluation practice into activity design and delivery; regular reporting through governance committees and student partnership structures.
supporting_quote: We take a full lifecycle approach to supporting our HE students from pre-entry, where we deliver summer schools and academic writing workshops, to post graduation, where we continue to offer access to our employability team up to 3 years after graduating. ... We will recruit ‘Widening Participation Fellows’ directly from the intervention groups to be the voice of their programme... The ‘Widening Participation Fellows’ will also sit on our Student Partnership and Engagement Committee (SPEC)... ongoing monitoring and evaluation of our intervention strategies... embedding evaluation into activity design and delivery... working in partnership with student representatives... SEER membership provides evaluation and research expertise.

student_group: students eligible for Free School Meals (FSM)
intervention: Junior Evolve Programme: A sustained, progressive programme delivered to students in Year 5 and 6, and Year 7-11 in schools with high FSM proportions; includes academic sessions and IAG to increase knowledge and awareness of benefits of HE and graduate employment.
intended_outcome: Increased student knowledge and awareness of HE benefits, increased capacity to navigate HE and graduate employment sectors, and make informed choices.
evaluation_approach: Pre and post questionnaires with school students (Type 2), teacher surveys (Type 1), and HEAT Tracking for long term evaluation of enrolment to HE.
supporting_quote: 1.1 Junior Evolve Programme: A sustained, progressive programme of activity delivered to students in Year 5 and 6, and Year 7-11 in schools with high proportions of FSM students. The programme includes sessions focused on core subjects, introduction to HE, academic sessions and IAG. Increased student knowledge and awareness of the benefits of higher education and graduate employment. Increased student capacity to navigate higher education and graduate employment sectors and make informed choices. Pre and post questionnaires with school students used to measure progress against activity outcomes (Type 2). Surveys used with teachers to generate feedback (Type 1). HEAT Tracking for long term evaluation of enrolment to HE.

student_group: students of low and high socioeconomic status (TUNDRA Q1 & 2, IMD Q1 & 2 and eligible for FSM)
intervention: Transition & induction programme for students entering through supported progression schemes and/or eligible students, including targeted study skills, employability support, wellbeing sessions including mental health, and peer mentoring.
intended_outcome: Improved study skills leading to increased academic attainment and successful graduate progression; improved engagement supporting continuation, attainment and completion; improved sense of belonging and career confidence.
evaluation_approach: Impact measurement via Civitas software (Type 2), module outcomes, progression to second year, longitudinal graduate outcomes, pre and post surveys, focus groups, Career Pulse survey.
supporting_quote: 2.1 To introduce a transition & induction programme for students who enter Northumbria through supported progression schemes and/or are eligible within this plan. This programme will include: Targeted Study skills sessions delivered by the library. Targeted employability support delivered by graduate futures. Targeted wellbeing sessions deliver by SLW colleagues, including mental health. Peer mentoring from previous supported entry students. Improved study skills > increased academic attainment and successful graduate progression; Improve engagement in studies > increased continuation; Improve engagement with services > increased continuation, attainment & completion; Improve sense of belonging > increased continuation & completion; Improve career confidence.

student_group: care experienced students, estranged students, and student carers
lifecycle_stage: entire lifecycle (access, continuation, completion, attainment, progression)
intervention: NU Belong Confident scheme to improve access to work experience opportunities, staff training targeted at personal tutors for better awareness and referral, community-engaged learning and enquiry with co-produced guides, peer support schemes, and financial support.
intended_outcome: More interview experience, better graduate outcomes and career confidence for students; improved staff awareness leading to more referrals and improved student experience; improved attitudes, sense of belonging, academic performance and progression through community-engaged learning.
evaluation_approach: Type 1: Focus groups and surveys for consultation and process evaluation; Number of referrals; Participation statistics; Type 2: tracking outcomes of involved students; publishing findings in edited volumes and journal articles.
supporting_quote: 3.6 Introduce a new NU Belong Confident scheme when recruiting for student roles on campus ... Provide more interview experience & more work experience for successful applicants > better graduate outcomes & career confidence. Type 1: Measured by career readiness data. Focus groups will provide consultation and process evaluation. 3.7 Staff training sessions relating to NU Belong targeted at Personal Tutors ... Improved staff awareness and understanding > more referrals > improved student experience and outcomes. Feedback forms following training Number of referrals by Tutors. 2.6 Community-engaged learning and enquiry ... Improve: students attitudes towards oneself, attitudes towards learning, civic engagement, social skills, academic performance, all leading to improved success & progression; Enhance sense of belonging via engagement in community-based learning > improved success outcomes. Type 1: Participatory evaluation through students & community partners collaborating on scholarship, publishing findings. Tracking outcomes of students engaged in project.
page_or_section: Pages 22-24, Intervention Strategy 3 (IS_3) and Community-engaged learning detail

student_group: Black students
intervention: PASS (Peer Assisted Study Skills) schemes implemented in targeted departments where Black student attainment gaps are identified; targeted transition and induction support; financial support.
intended_outcome: Eliminate gaps in student success (completion and attainment) between Black and White students; improve on-course and progression outcomes.
evaluation_approach: Use of Impact to measure retention (Type 2), tracked module outcomes, attendance; surveys and feedback; measured by engagement and continuation data.
supporting_quote: PASS (Peer Assisted Study Skills) schemes implemented in 3 targeted departments where Black student attainment gaps are identified. Eligible for targeted transition and induction support and financial support. Outcomes cross intervention. Method(s) of evaluation include Type 2 Use of Impact to understand impact on student retention and module outcomes.

student_group: Asian students
intervention: Improving access to work experience through targeted work experience opportunities including internships, placements and international mobility; tailored and targeted careers guidance and support; Employability Learning Fund (ELF); recruitment of Student Inclusion Consultants from Asian student group.
intended_outcome: Eliminate the progression gap between Asian and White students through improved career readiness and graduate outcomes.
evaluation_approach: Career readiness surveys, feedback from students engaged, engagement data and graduate outcomes data (Type 2).
supporting_quote: 5.1 Targeted work experience opportunities including internal and external internship and placements and international mobility opportunities. Employability Learning Fund (ELF) for tailored funding. Student Inclusion Consultants to recruit Asian students as paid SICs. Increased access to work experience opportunities > improved career readiness and graduate outcomes. Type 2: Measured by career readiness surveys, feedback survey from students engaged, engagement data and eventually graduate outcomes data.

student_group: male and female students
intervention: Peer Assisted Study Skills schemes in targeted departments addressing male student attainment gaps; community-led initiatives including young White men eligible for FSM; personal, academic and mental health support improvements; financial support to reduce cost pressures.
intended_outcome: Significantly reduce gaps in student success (continuation, completion and attainment) between male and female students by 2030.
evaluation_approach: Type 2 evaluation via Impact to measure retention and student outcomes; surveys and focus groups; tracking engagement and progression outcomes.
supporting_quote: PASS (Peer Assisted Study Skills) schemes implemented in 5 targeted departments where Male student attainment gaps are identified. Community-led initiatives outlined in intervention activity 4.2 will include young White men eligible for free school meals as a target group. Intention to improve personal, academic and mental health support and reduce cost pressures. Evaluation includes Type 2 Impact to understand impact on student retention and outcomes.

student_group: Wide range of WP (widening participation) students
intervention: Peer support schemes centrally managed but locally owned, paid on-campus work experience opportunities to reduce financial barriers and improve belonging and academic identity, co-creation of initiatives with students, community-engaged learning and enquiry, targeted information, advice and guidance (IAG) integrated with other support forms.
intended_outcome: Improve continuation, attainment, progression and student mental health by enhancing self-efficacy, belonging, academic skills, career confidence and reducing financial barriers.
evaluation_approach: Mixed methods including student surveys, focus groups, interviews, longitudinal tracking of student outcomes, publication of findings in journals and edited volumes, use of Impact software, and process evaluation.
supporting_quote: Peer support is acknowledged widely as a route to support students at various stages of their student journey. Depending on the type of peer support implemented, the impact can be positive for a variety of outcomes… The creation of a central model could also link to deliverable 6 with ringfenced funding to pay student mentors/leaders for the relevant schemes. Paid on campus work experience… may have a positive impact on multiple outcomes and reduce a number of risks… Co-creation (FA10) Students as partners, producers and co-creators is a growing area of research… Evidence suggests multi-intervention outreach supports increased attainment and progression. Information, advice and guidance (IAG) interventions can positively impact student progression when integrated and tailored.
page_or_section: Pages 23-26, Annex B and relevant intervention strategy sections

student_group: ABMO students
intervention: School Outreach - Outreach in targeted geographical schools/colleges; Leadership Residential regional programmes; Horizon Broadening Programme careers and HE information, advice and guidance; Peer positive reinforcement through mentoring and positive role models; Community outreach and subsidised access to recruitment events; Post-recruitment targeted academic, orientation, and careers support.
intended_outcome: Increase the percentage of ABMO students in the TU student population by 2% by 2029; increase participation and awareness of HE and career pathways; improve confidence and progression to HE.
evaluation_approach: Type 2 evaluation including desk-based analytic trends, participant feedback, confidence survey; Type 3 evaluation with three-year causality focus groups on progression to HE and first year experience; internal and external reporting with ethics approval.
supporting_quote: 4.1 Intervention strategy 1: ABMO Access - To increase the percentage of ABMO students in the TU student population by 2% by 2029... Activities include school outreach, leadership residentials, careers and HE IAG, peer mentoring and role models, community engagement, and post recruitment support... Evaluation includes Type 2 and Type 3 methods with internal and external reporting

student_group: Students with diagnosed mental health conditions
intervention: 24/7 Student Assistance Programme; Triage Model for mental health support access; Disability Co-ordinator Structure for academic and pastoral support; Student Life mental health events; Counselling call-out contract; Residential transition events; Staff training and skills development; Volunteering for mental health; University Mental Health Charter adoption.
intended_outcome: Remove gaps in continuation, completion, and attainment compared to students with no known disability; reduce demand for crisis interventions; improve academic performance and wellbeing; increase social networks and life satisfaction; increase staff and student awareness and confidence.
evaluation_approach: Theory of change mapping; Type 2 methods (focus groups, surveys, service engagement analytics); Type 3 methods (comparative student outcome analyses, trial pilots); internal and external reporting including publications and sector collaborations.
supporting_quote: 4.2 Intervention strategy 2: Mental Health Success - To remove the gaps in continuation, completion, and attainment for students with diagnosed mental health conditions when compared to TU students with no known disability by 2029... Includes 24/7 support, triage, coordinators, events, counselling, training and volunteering... Evaluation includes Type 2 and Type 3 methods with sector partnerships and publications

student_group: Students with social and communication disabilities
intervention: Targeted student success support; Student Life programme of autism awareness events; Residential transition events; Staff training and skills development; Creation of dedicated online resource space for disabilities.
intended_outcome: Significantly reduce the gap in continuation rates compared to students with no known disability; increase awareness and visibility of support services; improve academic continuation.
evaluation_approach: Type 2 methods including training impact survey, confidence surveys, engagement monitoring, and student outcome trend analyses; Type 3 comparative trend analyses; internal and external reporting including publications and sector collaborations.
supporting_quote: 4.3 Intervention strategy 3: Social and Communication Disabilities Continuation - To significantly reduce the gap in continuation rates between students with social and communication disabilities when compared to TU students with no known disability by 2029... Activities include targeted support, awareness events, residential stays, training, and online resources... Evaluation as per section 7.0 and Annex B with Type 2 and Type 3 methods

student_group: Students with cognitive and learning disabilities
intervention: Dyslexia guidance enhancements; Online training module for staff on interacting with students with learning, cognitive or social & communication conditions; Online resource space; Student Life dyslexia awareness events; Adoption of Compassionate and Inclusive Curriculum approach; Intuitive learning tools.
intended_outcome: Significantly reduce the gap in attainment rates; increase staff awareness and confidence in signposting; enhance academic performance and progression; increase use of learning tools.
evaluation_approach: As per section 4.3 including training impact surveys, stakeholder confidence surveys, engagement analytics and student outcome analyses; internal and external reporting.
supporting_quote: 4.4 Intervention strategy 4: Cognitive and Learning Disabilities Attainment - To significantly reduce the gap in attainment rates between students with cognitive and learning disabilities when compared to TU students with no known disability by 2029... Includes dyslexia guidance, training modules, online resources, awareness events and curriculum approach... Evaluation as described in 4.3

student_group: Graduates from TUNDRA Q1 and Q2 backgrounds
intervention: Tees Valley Progress Project mentoring scheme; Funded graduate internships with SMEs; Graduate Coaches providing employability support; Summer internships program.
intended_outcome: Significantly reduce progression gap for TUNDRA Q1 graduates and remove gap for Q2 graduates compared to Q5 graduates by 2032; raise aspirations; increase professional networks; improve employability skills; increase graduate employment.
evaluation_approach: Type 2 methods including mentee focus groups, trend analyses, employer satisfaction and progression surveys, impact assessments; Type 3 comparative employability and graduate outcomes analyses; internal and external reporting with sector collaborations.
supporting_quote: 4.5 Intervention strategy 5: TUNDRA Q1&2 Progression - To significantly reduce the gap in progression rates for graduates from TUNDRA Q1 and to remove the gap in progression rates for graduates from a Q2 background by 2032... Includes mentoring, internships, graduate coaching and summer internships... Evaluation includes Type 2 and Type 3 methods with internal and external reporting

student_group: Graduates with a diagnosed mental health condition
intervention: Mentoring, internships, work experience programmes aligned similarly to 4.5 but targeted at mental health declared students. Total investment £456,000 p.a.
intended_outcome: Significantly reduce the gap in progression rates compared to students with no known disability by 2032.
evaluation_approach: Aligned with evaluation in 4.5 using Type 2 and Type 3 methods; comparative analyses; internal and external reporting.
supporting_quote: 4.6 Intervention strategy 6: Mental Health Progression - to significantly reduce the gap in progression rates for graduates with a diagnosed mental health condition by 2032. Link to IS1 and IS5. Evaluation aligns with 4.5. Total cost per year £456,000

student_group: Pre-16 students and school staff in the Tees Valley
intervention: Regional pre-16 programmes to increase HE attendance: digital upskilling for school staff; workshops and events targeting primary and secondary pupils including STEM days, Arts events, digital skills training.
intended_outcome: Improve regional opportunities for pre-16 students to attend HE by 2028; reduce attainment gap in the North East compared to national average; increase digital skills utilisation in classrooms.
evaluation_approach: Theory of change; Type 2 methods including engagement trend analysis, comparative pilots, participant questionnaires pre/post activity; internal and external reporting with interim and final reports.
supporting_quote: 4.7 Intervention strategy 7: Pre-16 Attainment - To improve regional opportunities and reduce attainment gap by 2028 and increase school staff digital upskilling... Activities include targeted events and training for pupils and staff. Evaluation uses Type 2 methods with staged reporting.

student_group: All students
lifecycle_stage: Whole student lifecycle - governance and evaluation
intervention: Establishment of an Equality of Opportunity Project team including data analyst, project manager, student leaders, and administrative support to deliver and evaluate the APP 2024-2028; embedding equality and opportunity governance and annual reporting aligned to APP targets.
intended_outcome: Deliver the Access & Participation Plan 2024-2028 with effective governance, transparency, and continuous improvement; embed equality of opportunity in University culture and practices.
evaluation_approach: Development of data dashboards; annual internal and external reporting; dissemination via multiple networks; theory of change aligned evaluation; sharing successes and learning sector-wide.
supporting_quote: Create a central Equality of Opportunity Project Team, including data analyst, project manager, student leaders and administrative support... Delivery of the Access & Participation Plan 2024-2028... Publication via TU LTExChange dedicated EoO online space, University Alliance network, TASO, OfS repository. Evaluation strategy is centered on theory of change mapping and collaborative dissemination 【4:4†Teesside University_APP_2024-25_V1_10007161.pdf the plan and Governance

student_group: Male students
intervention: Identify and address specific academic and non-academic needs of male students; provide mentorship and support systems tailored to male students; implement strategies to promote a culture of inclusivity and equity where male students feel valued and supported.
intended_outcome: Reduce the attainment gap between male and female students from 8.8% to 3.0% by 2028-2029, early identification and tailored interventions, successful academic integration, better engagement and wellbeing.
evaluation_approach: Activities 1.4 and 1.5 evaluated to OfS type 2 standard; use Student Perception Survey (SPS) with new branching questions from 2024-2025 to measure engagement and impact; results reported to Learning, Teaching and Quality Committee, Planning & Partnership Group, Principalship, Academic Board and Corporation Board.
supporting_quote:
This intervention strategy has three key aims: 1. Identify and address specific academic and non-academic needs of male students to enhance their engagement and success; 2. Provide mentorship and support systems tailored to the unique challenges and aspirations of male students; and 3. Implement strategies to promote a culture of inclusivity and equity within the School environment, where male students feel valued, supported and empowered to excel in their creative work.

The School will introduce branching questions in 2024-2025 on the theme of academic support to measure the engagement and impact of activities 1.4 and 1.5. The responses will provide a baseline to measure future cohorts against. The SPS results will continue to be reported through the School's committee structure.

student_group: Male students
intervention: Establish monitoring and tracking system for academic progress; FE/HE transition events; academic mentorship programme pairing male students with experienced mentors.
intended_outcome: Improve transition from FE to HE for male students; provide early identification and tailored support.
evaluation_approach: Not stated explicitly; linked to overall evaluation of intervention strategy 1.
supporting_quote:
1.2 Monitoring and Tracking (new activity): Establish a comprehensive system for monitoring and tracking the academic progress of male students.
1.3 FE/HE Transition Events (new activity): Providing guidance, resources and support for a smooth transition from FE.
1.4 Academic Mentorship Programme (new activity): A target academic mentorship programme pairing male students with experienced mentors.

student_group: Male students
intervention: Academic skills workshops focusing on study skills, time management and academic writing tailored to male students; extracurricular activities and community initiatives to promote belonging and social support.
intended_outcome: Equip male students with essential academic tools and improve wellbeing and motivation.
evaluation_approach: Activities 1.4 and 1.5 evaluated; SPS used for impact measurement.
supporting_quote:
1.5 Academic Skills Workshops (Ongoing activity): Academic skills workshops focusing on study skills, time management and academic writing – tailored to the needs of male students.
1.6 Extra curricular activity (Ongoing activity): Extracurricular activities and School/community initiatives to promote a sense of belonging, connection and social support.

student_group: Female students
intervention: Meet female students’ needs in entering creative industries; expand career prospects and job access; support confidence, negotiation skills, resilience; bridge education and employment gap through mentoring, networking and targeted support.
intended_outcome: Reduce progression gap from 18.1% to 2% by 2028-2029; increase successful transition to graduate employment; improve retention and representation of female graduates in creative industries.
evaluation_approach: Informal feedback gathered from network events and piloted activities; SPS branching questions introduced in 2024-2025 to measure engagement and impact; results reported through School committees.
supporting_quote:
This intervention strategy has four key aims: 1. Meet the needs and aspirations of female students, helping them navigate the challenges of entering the creative industries; 2. Expand the career prospects and access to job opportunities for female students; 3. Support female students to build confidence, negotiation skills, and resilience to overcome gender biases and stereotypes in the workplace; and 4. Bridge the gap between education and employment for female graduates.

Evaluation: Informal feedback will be gathered from activities 2.1, 2.3 and 2.4, particularly as 2.4 is piloted in 2024-2025. Branching questions in SPS will measure engagement with activity 2.2 with results reported to committees.

student_group: Female students
intervention: Creative Industry Network Events for female students and alumni to attend; collaborative events with external industry experts to enhance mentoring and professional networking.
intended_outcome: Increase access to jobs, collaborations, ongoing support; improve confidence and negotiation skills; enhance retention in creative industries.
evaluation_approach: Informal feedback; part of overall monitoring through Student Perception Survey and committee reports.
supporting_quote: 2.1 Creative Industry Network Events (New Activity): Female students and alumni to attend Creative Industry Network Events. Collaboration with external industry experts. Resources and staff provided for various workshops and events. Staff time funded through APP.

student_group: Economically disadvantaged students
intervention: Digital Skills Audit engaging economically disadvantaged students; enrichment through creative industry-based projects and visits.
intended_outcome: Improve digital skills and engagement; provide enrichment to support progression.
evaluation_approach: Not explicitly stated.
supporting_quote:
2.5 Digital Skills Audit (ongoing activity): Economically disadvantaged students engaging with skills audit and intervention sessions.
2.6 Enrichment: Economically disadvantaged students engaging with creative industry-based projects and enrichment opportunities (creative industry visits).
page_or_section: Activities related to progression and employability (page 15)

student_group: All students, particularly those underrepresented and with various characteristics
intervention: Use of Interim Examination Boards, Learning, Teaching and Quality Committee, and other School committees to monitor academic attainment and progress against APP targets; dissemination of findings on website, social media, CPD events, and national conferences.
intended_outcome: Ongoing monitoring and enhancement of the APP; improved attainment and progression through evidence-based actions.
evaluation_approach: Continuous monitoring via Interim Examination Boards and committee reports; annual reports including APP progress; dissemination and publication of findings; use of student surveys (NSS and SPS).
supporting_quote:
The School will continue to use Interim Examination Boards to monitor academic attainment by student characteristics. The School’s Learning, Teaching and Quality [LTQ] committee will continue to monitor progress against APP outcomes. Through the LTQ committee, the School produces an Annual Report considering progress against APP targets, continued throughout the lifecycle of this APP.
The School will disseminate and publish the evaluation of findings on the School’s website and social media platforms and explore opportunities to present findings at a national level through conferences and sector network groups.

student_group: socio-economically disadvantaged students
intervention: Three interventions: a pre-16 multi-intervention programme, a multi-intervention Key Stage 5 and transition programme, and a project to develop academic transition activity. These include information, advice and guidance, campus visits, academic skills development, near-peer mentoring, participation in The Brilliant Club’s Scholars Programme, guaranteed contextual offers, financial support, and first year coaching.
intended_outcome: Increased attainment, access, and continuation rates for socio-economically disadvantaged students.
evaluation_approach: Tracking student uptake and progression; enhanced theories of change; pre-post comparison of survey data; qualitative research; evaluation of cognitive and psychosocial outcomes such as academic self-efficacy, HE knowledge, and sense of belonging.
supporting_quote: Our interventions: This intervention strategy contains three different interventions: a pre-16 multi-intervention programme, a multi-intervention Key Stage 5 and transition programme, and a project to develop academic transition activity. These three interventions will work together to ensure increased attainment, access, and continuation for socio-economically disadvantaged students... The pre-16 multi-intervention programme ... combines information, advice and guidance, campus visits, academic skills development, and near-peer mentoring. Students will also take part in The Brilliant Club’s Scholars Programme twice during the programme... The KS5 and transition programme will include subject-related activity, a residential, near-peer mentoring, application support, academic skills development, university preparation, guaranteed contextual offers, financial support, and guaranteed first year coaching.

student_group: Asian heritage students
intervention: Expansion of the Elephant Access Programme partnership to Midlands and London hubs to engage 1,130 students annually, including Asian heritage students, providing information, advice and guidance, campus visits, and academic skills support; plus a bespoke multi-intervention KS5 and transition programme including subject-specific activity, residential, near-peer mentoring, application support, academic skills development, university preparation, financial support, guaranteed contextual offers, and first year coaching.
intended_outcome: Increased academic self-efficacy, knowledge of HE, sense of belonging, improvements in attainment at KS5, and increased progression to Durham University and HE in general.
evaluation_approach: Robust and frequent evaluations of programme effectiveness; monitoring impact and sharing findings with the sector.
supporting_quote: The Elephant Access programme is a multi-intervention programme that includes IAG, campus visits, and academic skill support... We will grow our partnership to include The Elephant Group’s Midlands and London hubs, which typically see high proportions of Asian student participation... Multi-intervention KS5 and transition programme ... will include subject-specific activity, a residential, near-peer mentoring, application support, academic skills development, and university preparation activity. The transition phase will include guaranteed contextual offers, financial support at Durham University, and guaranteed first year coaching. However, the specific activity included within this intervention will be co-designed together with a panel of Asian-heritage Durham University staff and students.

student_group: Black heritage students
intervention: Enhanced and expanded multi-intervention KS5 and transition programme, including subject-specific activity, residential, near-peer mentoring, application support, academic skills development, financial incentives, guaranteed contextual offers, financial support and guaranteed first year coaching; co-designed with Black heritage staff and students; plus a programme to collate and review evidence on Black student experience and create an action plan to address awarding gaps; culturally sensitive counselling partnership with a community-based charity.
intended_outcome: Increased academic self-efficacy, knowledge of HE, sense of belonging; improvements in attainment-related outcomes; increased progression and participation in HE; reduction in completion and awarding gaps.
evaluation_approach: Monitoring and evaluation of multi-intervention programme's impact to understand effectiveness and sharing findings; recurrent review of evidence and monitoring implementation of delivery plan; tracking awareness of culturally sensitive counselling support via surveys and service figures.
supporting_quote: Durham University’s intervention strategy for Black students spans across school and university life:... The intervention expands on the existing Space to Explore Potential (STEP) programme... The intervention will be delivered by the Schools, Outreach and Widening Participation Team... By the end of 25/26, collate and review the recent body of staff- and student-generated evidence on the Black student experience at Durham... Durham University partners with Nilaari, a Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic led community-based charity, to provide access to culturally appropriate mental health support for students.

student_group: Students with a reported disability
intervention: Bespoke transition support days for students needing routine/stability or socialising assistance; enhanced student support model with disability representatives in each department; partnerships with NHS services for mental health support; mental health support website and mind management workshops based on CBT principles; culturally sensitive counselling; staff autism and mental health awareness training and expanded support groups for ADHD/autism students.
intended_outcome: Decreased continuation and awarding gaps, improved mental health support, increased confidence, knowledge of support services, and sense of belonging.
evaluation_approach: Tracking access to services and awarding gaps via multiple research types including pre-post surveys, qualitative interviews, quasi-experimental designs; reporting annually and through detailed reports spreading to 2029.
supporting_quote: We will develop and deliver bespoke transition to Durham days... Enhanced student support model... Various links and partnerships with NHS services... mental health support website... mind management workshops based on CBT principles... Durham University partners with Nilaari, a Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic led community-based charity... Staff training on autism awareness and mental health conditions... further support groups for students with ADHD or autism.

student_group: Mature students
intervention: Creation of a dedicated mature learners coordinator role for pastoral support, navigation of university structures, signposting specialist services; creation of a support network of staff and peers run with Mature Students’ Association, holding events to foster belonging and build relationships.
intended_outcome: Increased sense of belonging, confidence in study skills, and confidence that support is available to complete studies successfully.
evaluation_approach: Pre-post comparison survey data on sense of belonging and study skills; qualitative research including interviews and focus groups; annual publication of evaluation reports.
supporting_quote: Create a central support capability for mature students, and at least one role to coordinate, advocate for and represent mature students... The development of this network will be led by the Mature Learners coordinator, in collaboration with Durham University Mature Students’ Association. This network will have a supportive function for mature students, as well as running regular events to foster belonging and build staff-student relationships.

student_group: All identified priority groups
lifecycle_stage: All lifecycle stages; focus on belonging
intervention: Overarching intervention strategy focusing on increasing sense of belonging across all priority student groups; incorporates elements across previous strategies and specific programs to foster belonging.

supporting_quote: We will maximise the use of technology to host transition events and introduce follow-up with potential students to ensure support is in place early. Promotion of early DSA application is vital to reduce delays in support setup. Early familiarisation has been identified as key for transition and continuation.

student_group: Students from ethnic minority groups with mental health issues
intervention: Shine A Light Project to understand lived experience and remove barriers to declaration of mental health issues
intended_outcome: Improve access to support services and reduce barriers related to mental health in ethnic minority students
evaluation_approach: Collection and analysis of lived experience, student voices and engagement to inform interventions
supporting_quote: This project will provide understanding of the lived experience of studying as a student from a minoritised ethnic group with mental health issues. It aims to remove barriers to declaration and increase access to services.
page_or_section: Section Shine A Light Project (7.3), pp. 15-16

student_group: All students with declared mental health conditions
intervention: Mental Health Charter and Out of Hours Support partnering with Home Group to provide accessible crisis support and wellbeing interventions
intended_outcome: Enhanced mental health support, crisis response, and proactive wellbeing measures leading to improved continuation and completion rates
evaluation_approach: Use of mental health survey data, referrals data, and ongoing quality improvement guided by Charter expectations
supporting_quote: The University Mental Health Charter includes analysis of provision and development activities. Out-of-hours support service, established in partnership with Home Group, handles crisis calls and aims to expand provision without compromising crisis capacity. Over 1,300 individuals referred to support in 2022/23 with 85% mental health. Ongoing data collation and survey to inform service improvements.
